claims.claim: Python repeatedly tests a while condition and executes its suite while that expression is true; if it is false, the loop terminates.
A break in the while suite terminates the loop without running its else suite.
A continue in a while suite skips the rest of that suite and returns to testing the expression.
A normal terminating while loop needs its body to change relevant state so its condition can eventually become false; otherwise it can repeat forever.
An update such as x = x + 1 requires prior initialization because Python evaluates the right-hand side before assigning the left-hand name.
The lesson's countdown produces [2, 1, 0] and stops after three executions.
